## Learning from data

A growing course book for asking good questions, choosing useful representations, and supporting conclusions with evidence. Read the explanations, explore an activity, and check your reasoning against worked solutions.

## One dataset, three views

The quantitative-data chapters use a **hypothetical sample of 24 students' one-way commute times**, recorded in whole minutes. This is separate from the 40-response School A travel-method survey in the foundations sequence. Changing a display does not change its observations.

<div data-chart="commute-dot" class="chart-frame"><p>Commute times: 5, 8, 10, 12, 12, 14, 15, 16, 18, 18, 20, 20, 22, 24, 25, 26, 28, 30, 32, 35, 38, 42, 48, 58 minutes.</p></div>

## How to study with this book

Read an explanation, predict what will happen, and then use the activity. For construction questions, draw on paper before opening **Show solution**. A correct answer includes appropriate labels, a sensible scale, and reasoning in context—not only arithmetic.

The activities run in your browser: no account, notebook kernel, or software installation is required. On a phone, open the chapter menu at the top. Your choices are not submitted to a teacher and are cleared when you reload the page. Printing shows reference states and expands solutions.

This is an evolving course resource, not yet a complete AP Statistics textbook. New chapters will extend the existing sequence rather than replace it. The source chapters, data, activity code, and tests are retained in the repository for future classes.
